title: Lindblad, Colapinto and Bortoleto to take penalties for US GP
excerpt:
Arvid Lindblad, Franco Colapinto and Gabriel Bortoleto have all been hit with grid penalties for this weekend's United States Grand Prix after they all exceeded the number of permitted power unit components.

Lindblad previously started at the back of the grid in Malaysia when Racing Bulls installed his fifth internal combustion engine (ICE) of the season, but they have opted to change this element again, marking his sixth of the four allowed.

In the case of Colapinto, who is looking to reduce Alpine's deficit to midfield rivals Racing Bulls, he received a new control electronics unit – his fourth of the campaign.

Audi have made the most alterations to Bortoleto's car, with the Brazilian taking his fourth energy store unit and fourth control electronics unit. A replacement ICE, turbocharger, exhaust set and power unit ancillary component have also been introduced but remain within the allocation, so won't influence his penalty.

As per the regulations, the first time the allocation of any power unit element is exceeded, a 10-place grid penalty will be applied, with the second time this occurs (and so on) resulting in a five-place grid drop – all penalties at the same event applying in a cumulative manner.

If a driver incurs a penalty exceeding 15 grid places, they will be required to start the race at the back of the field regardless.

Lindblad will take a five-place penalty while Colapinto will lose 10 positions from his Qualifying result, with Bortoleto likely to start at the back of the grid with his 20-place drop.

Qualifying for the United States Grand Prix gets underway at 1600 local time on Saturday, with lights out in Austin taking place at 1500 on Sunday.

title: Leclerc fastest in first practice for the United States GP
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc topped the times during the opening practice session for the United States Grand Prix, the Ferrari man setting the pace ahead of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen and McLaren’s Lando Norris.

The Mercedes duo of George Russell and Kimi Antonelli were fourth and fifth respectively – with the young Italian having the chance to potentially seal his maiden title this weekend – while Leclerc’s Ferrari team mate Lewis Hamilton settled for sixth.

With the drivers keen to get going at the Circuit of The Americas, Alpine’s Franco Colapinto led the pack out as the session got underway at 1230 local time. Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto and Cadillac’s Colton Herta – taking the seat of Sergio Perez for FP1 – were both sporting large aero rakes at the start as they sought to gain valuable data.

As the lap times started to come in, with the track bathed in Texas sunshine, there was initial concern from Verstappen over the radio about his steering as he reported to his team that there was “some kind of friction” while turning left. However, it didn't seem to hinder the four-time champion as FP1 continued.

With a quarter of the session gone it was Leclerc who topped the initial times after posting a lap just 0.074s faster than team mate Lewis Hamilton on the medium tyre. Much had been made about the upgrades the Scuderia had brought to Austin with the signs looking promising.

Meanwhile Russell was reporting back to his Mercedes team to check the front wing, citing that he suddenly experienced lots of understeer. Soon after, however, the Briton posted a time good enough for fifth on the hard compound, just behind his team mate Antonelli who had elevated himself to fourth on the same tyre.

As FP1 ticked past the halfway stage more drivers bolted on the soft tyre as the time for hot laps arrived, with Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg – one of the first to post a lap time on the C4 – reporting a weird noise from his PU on his effort.

Leclerc continued to impress on the softs, cementing his position at the top with an improved 1m 36.052s time while Hamilton was nearly eight tenths back on his initial attempt having gone wide onto the dusty part of the track.

Verstappen then got in on the act at the top of the timesheets, initially splitting the two red cars before going fastest with a 1m 35.862s – though that time was subsequently deleted for track limits at Turn 19. That left the Red Bull man back in second as Norris, Russell and Antonelli slotted into third, fourth and fifth respectively.

Hadjar and Lawson also lost lap times to track limits, as the drivers experimented with how far they can push the racing line on the circuit.

With the time continuing to tick down neither Williams car had set a lap time, the team reporting that the duo had only been doing data collection runs, before Sainz and Albon eventually posted times good enough for 19th and 20th.

The action then slowed down in the final stages with the majority of the field focusing on higher-fuel, race simulation runs leaving Leclerc top of the order as the chequered flag fell. Verstappen was second with Norris, Russell, Antonelli, and Hamilton completing the top six.

Oscar Piastri was seventh, with Gabriel Bortoleto an eye-catching eighth for Audi ahead of the Racing Bulls pair of Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson. Ollie Bearman was 11th for Haas with Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll taking 12th and 13th respectively ahead of the Red Bull of Isack Hadjar – who fell victim to track limits on more than one occasion.

Alpine’s Pierre Gasly was in P15, ahead of Esteban Ocon, Franco Colapinto, and Nico Hulkenberg. The Cadillac pair of Valtteri Bottas and Herta occupied P20 and P21 while Sainz remained in 19th and Albon was last, ultimately having his timed effort deleted.

The drivers and teams will now reconvene and examine their data before Free Practice 2 takes place at 1600 local time.

title: Can Alpine bounce back and take the P5 fight to Racing Bulls?
excerpt:
The battle between Racing Bulls and Alpine for fifth place in the World Championship has been one of the subplots of the 2026 season, and at the moment it’s advantage to the Italian team.

A strong run through the Azerbaijan, Bahrain and Singapore triple header saw Racing Bulls log 23 points, while Alpine scored none. It’s left the former with a handy advantage of 32 points with six rounds to go, including this weekend’s United States Grand Prix at COTA.

That’s a decent lead, but it’s not done yet, given that Alpine famously scored 33 points in a single soggy afternoon when Esteban Ocon and Pierre Gasly finished second and third at Interlagos in 2024.

The big frustration for the Enstone team is that the A526 has been competitive at every track, and often faster in Qualifying than the VCARB 03, but that hasn’t been translated into results – most infamously in Azerbaijan, where Franco Colapinto and Gasly collided.

In contrast, Racing Bulls have generally capitalised on their opportunities, notwithstanding the contact between Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson in the same event.

“There's been quite a few races we haven't really been as quick as them, but we've outscored them,” says the New Zealander. “Baku we got lucky, the team got lucky. And I feel like that outside of that, we've actually just done a really good job.”

Alpine’s challenge is to bounce back from the recent difficult run and score consistently over the remaining races.

“It's clear that we lost the last triple header, and we need to win this one,” says Colapinto. “We need a kind of stop, a reset, and a start from zero again. And it's tricky in F1 when everything comes very fast, and you have one weekend to another to another, and then you are in the sim.

“We were a long time in the factory four days after the race in Singapore, trying to find some performance for the future and trying to understand the issues we've got.

“I think in general again it's not to overanalyse anything, we don't need to go super into detail of every little bit, but generally it's been a couple of tough weekends.

“We mostly understand why. We also were not the luckiest, but you can clearly see it. So again, we'll need a bit of luck this last part of the year, but I'm sure we can do a good end of the season.”

It’s been a trend that the car has been more competitive over one lap than in race trim – related to tyre usage – although Colapinto suggests that the difference in form is perhaps not as marked as you might think.

“I feel like we've been competitive in general on Saturdays for sure,” he says. “On Sundays we've been strong as well. For the most part of the year, we were up there, and the races have been fighting for points. We look super strong.

“It's true that for me, Malaysia is tricky to say because of the weather, and the roughness of the track I think was something very specific. But then, in general Baku, Madrid, the hot races, we were in this very hot European season, and we were strong on Sundays. So I don't think it's something to be super concerned [about].

“I think we are normally stronger on Saturday than Sundays. That's a reality. But it's not that we are slow on Sundays. We are good, and we are looking to extract more pace of the car.”

Gasly says that the team isn’t doing anything fundamentally wrong, and the run of non-scores over the last triple header was just a sequence of unfortunate events.

“I think looking at Qualifying, we qualified in the Q3s in all three races, four including the Sprints,” says the Frenchman. “So the pace in quali has been good. In the race it was mixed bag of unlucky events – looking at the Baku race, in Sepang that was kind of like 50:50 with the starting tyre, and we got it wrong unfortunately, and Singapore, which I think unfortunately highlighted the main limitation of the car that we have in a race at the moment.

“So it was just all compacted in these three weeks, and obviously we've been very disappointed, because we had we lost a lot of ground to VCARB, and we expected quite a lot more points at the end of it.”

Gasly insists that P5 isn’t lost – and he’s hoping that history repeats.

“I think personally, I just want to take it race-by-race,” he says. “It's a big gap. At the same time, with that team I've seen back in 2024 we've had that amazing double podium in Brazil, and all of a sudden we had plenty of points scored.

“So it's never impossible. It's a tough challenge, but I think we've just got to take one race at a time, trying to do the best job we can. And then we'll do the maths at the end of the year.”

title: Crawford set for Mexico City FP1 outing with Aston Martin
excerpt:
Jak Crawford will take the wheel of Lance Stroll’s AMR26 during FP1 at the Mexico City Grand Prix, marking his fourth on-track appearance of the 2026 season.

Acting as Aston Martin’s Third Driver, Crawford drove in Free Practice sessions in Japan, Austria and Belgium and achieved a highest finish of P20 at the Red Bull Ring.

His upcoming FP1 running, announced during his home race weekend at the United States Grand Prix, will fulfil the team’s mandated rookie practice sessions for the year.

Since concluding his third campaign in Formula 2 last year, the 21-year-old has completed crucial testing and simulator work for the team as they sought to improve their underperforming power unit and chassis.

“I'm really looking forward to getting back behind the wheel of the AMR26 in Mexico City,” said Crawford, who joined the Aston Martin Driver Development Programme in 2024.

“It's a special circuit for me as it's where I made my FP1 debut last year, so it's great to return with more experience under my belt.

“I've learned a lot through my time on track and in the simulator this season, and I'm looking forward to putting that into practice.

“It's also special to be announcing this during my home race weekend in Austin. As always, the focus will be on making the most of the session and delivering useful feedback for the team.”

Chief Trackside Officer Mike Krack added: “We are pleased to give Jak another opportunity in the AMR26. He returns to Mexico City with considerably more experience than when he made his FP1 debut there last year.

“His contributions through our simulator and testing programmes have been valuable, and this session provides another opportunity to demonstrate his capabilities while supporting the team's preparations for the weekend.”

title: McLaren drivers 'still allowed to race' each other – Norris
excerpt:
Lando Norris has offered an update on McLaren's intra-team orders ahead of the United States Grand Prix, after the reigning World Champion and team mate Oscar Piastri collided at the previous round in Singapore.

Norris and Piastri collided on the final lap of the Sprint, with Norris ultimately accepting responsibility for the incident despite the stewards deciding it was a racing incident.

Speaking on Thursday's media day in Austin, Norris revealed that both he and Piastri would be able to race each other, but that any repeat collision would not be tolerated.

"I got plenty of telling-offs, and plenty of words have been said. But we’re still allowed to race," said Norris.

"But of course, we can’t have what happened last weekend, or what happened here last year [where the pair collided at Turn 1 in the Sprint], happening again.

"So, no, we’re still allowed to race, but obviously we can’t have a coming together, and we have to avoid that at every opportunity possible."

McLaren have failed to match their form from the summer, where Norris claimed two victories in Hungary and the Netherlands, as well as three pole positions.

The Briton believes that despite finding more outright pace, McLaren need to build and design a car that is more drivable when pushed to the limit.

"This was a car in which putting together a Qualifying lap was almost impossible, and being as quick as we were was almost impossible," said Norris.

"I mean, I was on pole three times by, I don’t know, two hundredths of a second or something — or not even on pole. So, you know, it wasn’t like we were just winning everything and it was easy.

"The car was probably one of the hardest cars I’ve ever had to drive. But I was putting things together, driving well, and I could get away with it.

"But this isn’t a car you can win a championship with. I still believe a win is possible this year. We just need a quicker car now if we want to get another win.

"But going into next year, we need a car that’s a lot more drivable and easier to drive. Because, yeah, you cannot win a championship with how difficult the car is to drive at the minute."

title: Russell on how 2026 has ‘tested my character and resilience’
excerpt:
George Russell has explained how he approached a series of setbacks that “tested my character and resilience” this season, with the Briton conceding that “it’s a matter of when, not if” Kimi Antonelli seals the Drivers’ Championship.

After a superb start to the year, Russell fell behind his Mercedes team mate and watched as Antonelli’s lead gradually increased as an incompatibility with the car and reliability issues affected his own results.

Victories in Austria and Azerbaijan proved his progress, but with other teams overhauling their respective deficits to Mercedes through upgrades, his chance of winning a maiden title has largely slipped out of his hands.

Antonelli’s first opportunity of being crowned champion comes at this weekend’s United States Grand Prix and partly relies on Russell finishing ninth or lower, but the Briton was prepared to admit that he’s “not in the fight”.

“Whether it’s this weekend or next weekend, it’s a matter of when, not if, he clinches it,” he said. “That’s the reality of the fact. For me, it’s been a very unique season.

“I’ve had to look at myself in the mirror numerous times and think, ‘How do I want to bounce back from these blows?’. Do I just want to give up and accept the misfortune or the poor performances, or do I want to try to rectify things, make the most of it and control everything I can control?

“I can at least be proud of myself that I’ve always put up a fight and always done my utmost to keep myself in the fight. I’ve got a great team around me, and this won’t be my last shot when I’ve got a car beneath me that can fight for victory.

“At the end of this weekend, we’ll see what we can do. We’ll try to get Mercedes back on top because it’s been a while, and let’s see what the future holds.”

Russell and Antonelli are both set to continue racing for the Silver Arrows in 2027, giving the Briton confidence that he can learn from the challenges of this season and come back even stronger in the future.

Russell explained: “I wouldn’t necessarily say there’s a lesson as such, but there have been a lot of things I’ve adapted to and improved on through the struggles I’ve had. It’s been a season that has very much tested my character and resilience.

“I guess I’ve learned a lot about myself being in these moments, because I’ve never really found myself in this position in my career before. So I guess I can say those are the lessons I’ll take forward, and they’ll help me over the next 10 or 15 years of my career.

“I don’t really have any major feelings running through my body when I say that we’re no longer in the fight this season, because when I look back earlier in the year, the things that were keeping me up at night weren’t necessarily about the championship.

“It was more that my performance wasn’t where I wanted it to be. It was like, ‘Well, how am I going to get my performance back to the levels I know I’m capable of? What is it I need from the car? What do I need to change in my driving to get back on top of things?’

“And then, obviously, the misfortune just added salt to the wound. But I intend to be here for many, many, many years to come, and you can’t give up when you’re being kicked to the floor. You’ve got to bounce back. I can at least be proud that I’ve given it my all in that regard.”

title: Verstappen backs Mekies' Red Bull contract extension
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has backed Laurent Mekies' contract extension with Red Bull, but has cautioned those who expect the Dutchman to continue his winning form at this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

It was announced earlier this month that Mekies will remain as Red Bull's CEO and Team Principal until 2031, having joined from Racing Bulls in 2025.

After a slow start under the new-for-2026 regulations, which included building their own engines alongside Ford, Red Bull have shown signs of progress under Mekies' leadership, prompting the new deal.

"It's been great news I think for everyone," said Verstappen during Thursday's media day in Austin on Mekies' contract extension.

"He fully deserves it as well, he's a very hard worker and I think at times this year of course it has not been easy for him as well, but he's a good leader and I think also the atmosphere in the team is great, so it's only right to extend the contract."

Verstappen has claimed dominant victories in the previous two Grands Prix as Red Bull have become the in-form team during the 2026 campaign.

Despite the winning combination, Verstappen is cautious whether he will be able to secure a hat-trick of victories this weekend at COTA, with the venue different to those in Malaysia and Singapore.

"We had two really good weekends, which of course we're very happy with but that is no guarantee that the coming races are going to be like that as well," said Verstappen.

"We had two very hot and humid races and it seemed like also our engine was performing well in these kinds of conditions and now we go of course to a very dry race.

"There are a lot of factors that are a bit different but we'll see. We'll just take it step by step, we don't dream too much, we just stay in the current [frame of mind] and we also know that we want to improve a lot on the car that we can't fix or change for this year, but hopefully for next year."

title: Red Bull hide secret Max Verstappen update from prying eyes in Austin
excerpt:
Red Bull arrived at Circuit of the Americas for this weekend's United States Grand Prix without any major upgrades, continuing straight from back-to-back wins in Malaysia and Singapore with only marginal set-up tweaks on the car.

That made a small detail spotted in the Milton Keynes-based squad's pit lane during the standard Friday build-up all the more notable.

Mechanics were seen working on the front end of the car ahead of first practice, and were quick to screen off the installation of new Brembo brake discs, blocking photographers from getting a clear shot.

Further checks revealed the discs carry a new surface pattern, one that is no longer uniformly solid.

The change is expected to affect two things. The initial bite under braking is understood to remain similar to the previous specification, but the pattern has been tailored specifically to suit Max Verstappen's aggressive braking style, aiming for greater consistency through the full braking phase and across a race distance.

In practice, that should give the four-time F1 champion a wider operating window to extract maximum performance compared with a disc running a standard surface.

The development points to something bigger than a trackside tweak. It suggests Red Bull is already trialling solutions with half an eye on the 2027 regulations, while also underlining how closely the Austrian marque is now working with Brembo to fine-tune both the RB23 and the braking characteristics of the current RB22 around Verstappen's specific preferences.

It all feeds into a growing sense in the paddock that the RB22, once a difficult, unpredictable car in the first half of the campaign, has quietly turned into the benchmark that the rest of the grid is chasing.

title: Charles Leclerc hands Ferrari boost as Max Verstappen outpaced in Austin FP1
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc has ended the first practice session of the United States Grand Prix on top of the timesheet, setting a 1:36.052 behind the wheel of his Ferrari.

The Circuit of the Americas hosts the 18th round of the 2026 campaign, with Max Verstappen entering the race after securing back-to-back wins in Malaysia and Singapore.

However, the four-time champion had to settle for second on the timesheet at the end of FP1, less than one-tenth down on Leclerc.

Lando Norris was the leading McLaren car as he rounded out the top three.

[Article continues below]

Throughout the session, drivers struggled to keep their cars within the white lines, a common issue around the circuit in Austin.

As a result, many lap times were deleted as the drivers pushed to find the limit.

With the top three consisting of Leclerc, Verstappen and Norris, George Russell was fourth in his Mercedes.

He headed team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who enters the weekend with a chance to win the title for the first time.

Lewis Hamilton was sixth in the second Ferrari car, over half a second down on his session-leading team-mate.

Oscar Piastri was seventh for McLaren, ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto, who had a positive opening outing of the weekend for Audi, setting the eighth-fastest time.

The top was rounded out by Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson, with the two Racing Bulls targeting more points this weekend as it closes in on consolidating fifth in the constructors' championship.

Colton Herta was the only rookie driver to take part in the session as he jumped behind the wheel of Sergio Perez's Cadillac.

The American driver ended the session in 21st place, nine-tenths down on Valtteri Bottas.

He headed Alex Albon, whose only lap time came at the end of the session amid a test-focused outing for Williams.

title: Multiple F1 drivers handed grid penalties for United States Grand Prix
excerpt:
Arvid Lindblad, Gabriel Bortoleto and Franco Colapinto will all start the United States Grand Prix on Sunday with grid penalties.

The trio have taken on fresh power unit components outside of the mandated pool, ensuring they will drop down the order after qualifying at the Circuit of the Americas on Saturday.

Racing Bulls driver Lindblad will serve a five-place penalty for taking a sixth internal combustion engine, with only four allowed for the season. As it is a second 'offence', the sanction is five places, as opposed to 10 with the first change outside of the pool.

Audi driver Bortoleto faces a 20-place penalty, ensuring he will start at the back of the grid. The Brazilian's car has been burnished with a completely new PU.

Whilst the ICE, turbocharger and exhaust sets comply with the regulations, the energy store and control electronics are the fourth of the season, with only three permitted.

As for Colapinto, he will serve a 10-place penalty for a fourth control electronics.

title: F1 braced for 'whingy' drivers after 'always fun' reason identified
excerpt:
F1 commentator Alex Jacques has explained why the bumps at the Circuit of the Americas cause drivers to 'whinge' at the start of the United States Grand Prix weekend.

Jacques described how they "shift year to year", leaving the track surface unpredictable and fraught with jeopardy during FP1 and FP2 in Austin.

COTA has long been known for its bumps, and Max Verstappen pointed out earlier this year how difficult the asphalt looked when watching the Lone Star Le Mans race (formally the 6 Hours of COTA).

The four-time F1 drivers' champion further addressed the matter on media day in Austin, revealing the toll it takes on the body.

"Well, the bumps shift year to year, which is always fun, so you get whingy drivers on a Friday," Jacques explained on the F1 Nation podcast when detailing what lay in wait for the field this weekend.

"You've got a glorious overtaking opportunity at Turn 1. They copied Silverstone's homework for a lot of the rest of that sector, and all the better for it; it's a spectacular change of direction.

"Then you have another hairpin onto the long straight, another great overtaking opportunity down to Turn 12. Then you're into mechanical grip.

"Ferrari will be happiest through Turn 12, and then the slower stuff where you sometimes get a dive-bomb move, and then it's fast stuff.

"The pesky Turn 19 with track limits, and then you find yourself at the Andretti corner that completes it.

"It's a nice mix. It's a nice combination of defined overtaking zones and a real test of where the car's at, especially in that first sector."

[Article continues below]

Why COTA is a 'modern classic'

When it was put to Jacques that COTA is a modern classic F1 track, he expanded on his initial answer, highlighting the elevation changes and how much of a driver's circuit it is.

"It's brilliant," he agreed. "If you consider it was purpose-built, and as we've seen at some other venues, it's very difficult to get it right immediately when it comes to that.

"This is just a great layout. The undulation plays a massive part as well, and it requires a very, very strong all-round performance of the car.

"But it does tend to be a race track where the driver makes a difference by the end of Q3 as well, so it's a very, very good place to go racing.

"Notwithstanding, it's in a wonderful part of the world as well."

title: Oscar Piastri delivers McLaren verdict after 'serious' Lando Norris rule breach
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri is happy with the way in which McLaren has dealt with Lando Norris crashing into him in the Singapore Grand Prix Sprint.

On the penultimate lap at Marina Bay, Norris attempted to move up the inside of Piastri for fourth place, but misjudged the move and sent the Australian spinning into the barriers and out of the race, whilst Norris himself recovered to eighth place and picked up one point.

In total, McLaren lost seven points in the collision, which could prove crucial in the constructors' championship as the team is now just seven ahead of a resurgent Red Bull in the fight for third.

On the Saturday, team principal Andrea Stella laid out the seriousness with which he was treating the collision, with Norris initially taking a defiant stance, before this cooled after the race itself on Sunday.

After further talks and discussions between the drivers, Stella, and CEO Zak Brown, Piastri has declared himself satisfied with how the issue has been handled following the breach of so-called 'Papaya Rules.'

"I've been happy with how things have been dealt with," Piastri told media, including RacingNews365.

"I think the team, Zak and Andrea, have handled things the way they should have been, so that's been fine.

"Yes, I mean, it's been a challenging year for us, definitely. I think in the middle of the season we felt like we'd gained some momentum and potentially we were back to being able to fight for wins and regular podiums.

"But, yes, that's often the way in Formula 1. You think you're there again, and you've got a few teams around you to pull you down a few pegs.

"Hopefully we can find a bit more performance in the rest of the season. But, yes, I think in terms of going back to Singapore, I think it was dealt with appropriately, and we're ready to go racing."

[Article continues below]

Norris' response

As for Norris himself, he also declared that as far as he was concerned, the matter was "settled."

"I'm just fully focused on the weekend now. It's been settled," he said.

"Things have always been clear. It's just that I messed up, and I admitted already last time that I made a mistake. Things have always been settled.

"It's clear in my head what needs to be done, what can and cannot be done. Sometimes I make mistakes, so that's all it has been.

"Of course, there's been plenty of talk since then between everyone, of course, especially between Andrea, Zak and myself, and us as a group.

"But things have always been clear. Nothing really needed to be cleared up. It wasn't like I wasn't aware of what it was. It's just that I messed up, and I apologise for that."

title: Mercedes' F1 rivals strike back on fiercely-fought battleground
excerpt:
Mercedes' F1 rivals have brought a series of upgrades to the United States Grand Prix as the development battle intensifies at the Circuit of the Americas.

McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull have all introduced new components for the Austin weekend, while Mercedes has elected against bringing further updates.

Instead, the Brackley-based squad will focus on extracting the maximum performance from the upgrade package introduced two rounds ago at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, which has proven troublesome thus far.

According to the FIA's official car presentation submissions, Ferrari has delivered the most extensive package of the leading four teams, targeting improvements to the floor, sidepods and diffuser.

The Scuderia has revised its floor body and floor board, including the front floor's leading edge and supporting elements, to increase downforce at both ends of the car while improving airflow towards the rear.

Its revised sidepod inlet, undercut and coke-line geometry complement an updated diffuser, designed to generate additional aerodynamic load more efficiently.

McLaren has introduced three updates, comprising revised front and rear corner assemblies and a modified diffuser.

The front corner changes work alongside the suspension fairings to improve airflow, while the rear corner revisions target increased local load. The new diffuser geometry is intended to improve aerodynamic performance across the speed range.

Red Bull, meanwhile, has made two changes, including an additional vane on the front-wing endplate footplate.

The optional component allows tyre surface temperature measurements while offering increased local aerodynamic load.

A revised elastomeric gaiter profile at the front corner is also aimed at improving reliability by reducing the risk of material tearing under steering loads.

[Article continues below]

Racing Bulls lead midfield upgrade push

Racing Bulls has submitted four updates for Austin, targeting its front wing, rear wing, floor and engine cover.

A redesigned front-wing endplate improves airflow around the front tyres, while revised rear-wing flaps aim to generate additional load.

Changes to the floor's leading-edge devices, board and edge seek more efficient downforce, supported by a reprofiled engine-cover shoulder and undercut.

Audi has brought three updates, including a new front brake duct designed to improve cooling and aerodynamic performance.

A revised front floor board and mirror stay complete its package, both intended to improve airflow around the car.

Alpine has redesigned its rear floor corner to increase local load and improve airflow interaction with the rear corner.

It has also reprofiled the second and third rear-wing flap elements to improve airflow quality and overall aerodynamic load.

Cadillac has introduced revised forward floor fences to improve airflow towards the rear and reduce sensitivity to changes in car attitude.

Updated sidepod cooling louvres are also intended to increase power-unit cooling capacity while limiting aerodynamic losses.

Williams, Aston Martin and Haas have submitted no updates for the United States Grand Prix.

title: Max Verstappen brands Isack Hadjar debate 'nonsense' after eye-catching claim
excerpt:
Max Verstappen believes the debate around comments made by Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar and the Singapore GP is "nonsense."

On Thursday's media day in the United States, Hadjar claimed that if Verstappen had been driving the Ferrari SF-26 if Singapore, he would have won by a greater margin than the 7.3s he did over Charles Leclerc - as the Frenchman also claimed that the RB22 is not the fastest car on the grid.

Red Bull's recent upgrade in Azerbaijan has unlocked performance from the car, although Hadjar suffered a number of mechanical and technical issues at Marina Bay which did not allow him to contend at the head of the field.

In contrast, Verstappen claimed pole position in both the Sprint and grand prix, going on to win both for a dominant performance - at a track which was expected to suit Ferrari, with its car considered as the best through the corners.

Leclerc dismissed Hadjar's comments, with Verstappen also taking issue with other drivers being asked about the second-year driver's words.

"I mean, we're stressing about something that doesn't matter, right?" Verstappen countered to media, including RacingNews365, when asked for his thoughts on Hadjar's claim.

"Yeah, he said it, but okay, let him say that, right?

"I mean, you shouldn't always need to put it forward to the other driver or the other team as you do constantly, trying to agitate people with it instead of just letting it be.

"That's what I normally do; I'm like: 'Whatever, life goes on, and tomorrow is another day.'

"It was a good qualifying lap. I'm not going to say that it is anything special because it can always be better, but I felt good.

"I felt good with my car, and it is impossible for me to know or say how good a Ferrari is because I've not driven that car.

"And that is why these debates are just nonsense."

title: Historic F1 circuit set for remarkable 2027 motorsport arrival
excerpt:
A historic F1 circuit without a space on the 2027 calendar will welcome a different championship next year.

IndyCar has confirmed a historic addition to its 2027 calendar, with the NTT IndyCar Series set to race at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya for the first time.

The inaugural IndyCar Grand Prix of Barcelona is scheduled for Sunday, 18 July and will form the centrepiece of Phase Two of next year's schedule. It marks IndyCar's first visit to Spain and sets up what is being billed as a homecoming for Barcelona native Alex Palou, the five-time NTT IndyCar Series champion who races for Chip Ganassi Racing.

The multi-year deal with the Montmeló circuit represents IndyCar's first race outside North America since 2013, when James Hinchcliffe won on the streets of São Paulo. It also marks a return to Europe for the series, which last raced on the continent in 2007 at TT Circuit Assen in the Netherlands.

Penske Entertainment Corp. president and CEO Mark Miles described the announcement as a landmark moment for the championship.

"This is a monumental day for our sport," Miles said. "We are pleased to be able to take our ultra-competitive brand of wheel-to-wheel racing to Europe and thrilled that we can showcase IndyCar in Alex Palou's hometown. We have seen Alex's remarkable skill and talent for several years and know his fans in Spain have been clamouring to watch him race in person.

"We cannot wait to see the NTT IndyCar Series compete at one of the world's most recognisable motorsports venues set against the backdrop of a very historic and breathtaking international destination like Barcelona."

Palou sealed his fifth NTT IndyCar Series title in 2026, becoming only the second driver in the series' history to win four consecutive championships, joining Sebastien Bourdais, who achieved the feat between 2004 and 2007.

With five titles in six years and 25 career wins, the Spaniard is tied for 17th on the all-time wins list. Only A.J. Foyt, with seven championships, and Scott Dixon, with six, have won more.

Barcelona welcomes significant IndyCar arrival

Palou said he could not wait to race in front of his home crowd.

"I'm so excited to be part of IndyCar's first race in Barcelona," Palou said. "It is an amazing opportunity, and it means so much to me to have a race at home in Barcelona, it's hard to put into words. I know the fans are going to love it, and I think we are going to put on a great show.

"We're going to try hard with the team at Chip Ganassi Racing to bring home the trophy in July."

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located just outside the Spanish city, has hosted international motorsport since opening in 1991, including Formula 1 and MotoGP, and is known for its blend of high-speed corners and technical sections.

Chairman of the Board of Fira de Barcelona and Fira Circuit Pau Relat said the arrival of IndyCar was a significant moment for the venue.

"The arrival of IndyCar is a major milestone and an exciting challenge for the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya," Relat said. "Bringing one of the most prestigious and spectacular championships in global motorsport to our venue strengthens our international positioning, connects us with new audiences and markets, and reinforces our strategy of diversifying the circuit's activity through world-class events.

"We are working with a long-term vision to make IndyCar Grand Prix of Barcelona a benchmark event on the international racing calendar for years to come."

title: Lewis Hamilton explains why he overruled Ferrari F1 strategy instruction
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has explained his decision to overrule Ferrari's strategy during his doomed one-stop race in Singapore.

Starting on the mediums, Hamilton abandoned the strategy early at Marina Bay, after it became apparent that the softs were the favoured race tyre, and was faced with completing 44 laps on a set of the used red-marked rubber.

However, halfway through the stint, a virtual safety car was deployed, potentially handing Hamilton a free stop, with team-mate Charles Leclerc taking the opportunity, but Hamilton did not follow the team instruction to pit.

Ultimately, in the final 10 laps, he ran out of tyres as they fell off the cliff, dropping behind Kimi Antonelli, Lando Norris, and Oscar Piastri to finish sixth, as he took initial responsibility on the cooldown lap for the failure.

Hamilton then did not attend the written media pen session after reporting he felt unwell, with the FIA granting him permission not to attend after a medical check-up by doctors.

Therefore, speaking at length about the decision for the first time publicly, Hamilton explained that the decision not to pit under the VSC was a "split-second" call he got wrong.

"Firstly, you learn from these experiences, and it's rare that I find myself in that position," Hamilton told media, including RacingNews365.

"Of course, the next couple of days didn't feel so great, but you live, and you learn. I think when I was lining up on the grid, when I knew I was going to be third, I'm always looking at ways to win.

"I'm always looking at doing potentially something different, and I wanted to be on a different strategy, not just the same strategy as Charles, where we just follow each other. The strategy ultimately, we assumed that Max would be potentially quick, and the strategy showed us finishing second and third, and that's not enough for me.

"I wanted to have options and see what could be possible should the tyre last. If the medium tyre could last longer, maybe you go deeper into the race, but it wasn't the case when I got going, and it didn't feel great in the first stint.

"Then, obviously, coming out behind Charles and losing a lot of time with him on a slower tyre, which I was on at the beginning, and I had the pace on the Soft, it was a bit of a similar scenario to Zandvoort. But I think I was coming towards the pit lane entry and I didn't know Charles was coming in, because I think he'd only recently stopped.

"It was a split-second decision, and I decided to stay out. As soon as I was alongside the pit lane, I realised it was probably the wrong decision. But I owned up to it, took responsibility for it, and moved on."

[Article continues below].

Hamilton's Ferrari conversations

Turning to the conversations with the team between the two grands prix, Hamilton spoke of finding ways to "continuously challenge the team and the norms."

"We've had good conversations in the background about how we can do better together and how we can collaborate better," he added.

"But I think nothing's changed in terms of how well we work together in the background. I truly believe my job, rather than to follow suit always, is to continuously challenge the team and myself, including constantly challenging the norms.

"And that's ultimately how I've got to where I am. I will not shy away from that. Sometimes it doesn't go well, and that was one of those times.

"But you live to fight another day. And we win and lose as a team, so we carry the weight and the cost together. It definitely hurts when I lose points for the team.

"It's not something I do very often, but I'll double my efforts to make sure that doesn't happen again."

title: FIA detail ambitious plans to lower F1 car weight in rules overhaul
excerpt:
The FIA's single-seater technical director has explained plans to cut F1 car weights by nearly 70kg by the time of the next regulation cycle.

The maximum weight of the 2026 machines is 768kg, with this being a reduction of 30kg from the 798kg dry weight in 2025 at the end of the ground effects era.

By the end of the four-year cycle, the cars had ballooned in weight, in part due to the 18-inch wheel rims and bigger tyres, as well as the increased safety devices now used, including the cockpit protection and halo head protection device.

For the next rules cycle, it is clear that F1 will be returning to V8 engines and drop the turbo hybrids, with FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem hopeful this can happen by 2030 or 2031.

It is hoped through a concerted effort that car weights could drop below 700kg for the next rules cycle.

[Article continues below].

FIA's weight reduction hopes

Explaining the coming work to try to get cars back under 700kg, Tombazis explained where the hoped-for-savings would come from.

"We are looking to reduce turbo pressures significantly," Tombazis told The Race.

"That will reduce the pressures both inside the engine and the dimensions of the turbocharger.

"We plan to significantly reduce the complexity of both the inlet and the outlet of the engines - as currently they have a very complex 'spaghetti' of ducts leading into the engine.

"The exhausts are also all tuned for length and so on, so we plan to shorten and simplify those areas a lot."

With the heavy battery systems being dropped for the V8 engines as opposed to the V6 turbo hybrids, further weight savings are planned from this, with a reduction in wheel rim size also anticipated to bring sizeable savings.

Finally, it is hoped that cars will not be required to use as heavy aerodynamic parts when they are lighter and smaller, with this bringing a virtuous circle in terms of weight saving.

"When we do the shopping list and add everything up, we can get quite comfortably below 700kg," Tombazis added.

"Now we are conscious that when we discuss things, there will be some kickback in some areas. We'll have to compromise a bit.

"There will be concerns about certain costs, but overall our target is to be below 700kg, and I think it will be a significant step to make the cars more exciting."

Refuelling will not be reintroduced for the first time since 2009, owing to the added expense, complexity, and dangers of it, and the fact that it limits opportunities for strategic variance.

title: Lando Norris required to 'take tablets' to combat US Grand Prix health concern
excerpt:
Lando Norris has explained how he is required to take "headache tablets" to combat the effects of bumps at the United States Grand Prix venue, Austin.

The Circuit of the Americas was built for the 2012 race on former marshland near Austin Bergstrom International Airport, meaning the ground underneath the track is constantly being forced up and down, with the Texas climate also affecting the track surface.

It was not a concern prior to 2022, with the cars not being run as close to the ground as during the ground effects era of 2022-2025, where downforce was generated by running the car as close to the track surface as possible - thus amplifying the effect of the bumps.

On Thursday ahead of this year's race, Max Verstappen claimed that the bumps situation was "unacceptable" and spoke of the potential for severe spinal damage, having endured peak stresses of 9G at times in the 2025 race.

And Norris believes his fellow world champion Verstappen is "certainly right" with the criticism levied at the track surface.

"I would say yes," Norris told media, including RacingNews365, when presented with Verstappen's "unacceptable" comments.

"If you build a new track now, the FIA has the rules and regulations for building a new track and the tolerances you have to be within are pretty small.

"It certainly doesn't fit anywhere close to what the regulations are now, let's say, but it is an old track, not a new track.

"It is pretty bad, and there are places where I need to take headache tablets before I go out, simply because it is so bumpy and you are hitting your head against the headrests because of the bumps.

"So it is certainly not a nice thing, but there is not a lot we can do.

"We complain about it, and it is brought up many times, but there is only so much we can complain about things, but [Verstappen] is certainly right."

title: George Russell hints at F1 title fight acceptance as 'reality' picture painted
excerpt:
George Russell's team-mate Kimi Antonelli sits on the verge of his maiden F1 title, which he can clinch this weekend in the US.

George Russell has stated that his season wasn't "meant to be" as he sits on the verge of a title defeat to team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Antonelli enters the United States Grand Prix 102 points clear of Russell in the drivers' standings and has his first opportunity to seal the title on Sunday at the Circuit of the Americas.

Russell has faced several hurdles throughout the year, including some reliability woes that have cost him valuable points.

However, the Briton has admitted that in the early stages of the season, his performances were not up to scratch in the fight against Antonelli.

"In terms of my mentality this season, my view of the championship has been up and down," Russell told media including RacingNews365.

"Early in the year when I had a big point deficit, the thing that was keeping me up at night was my lack of performance and thinking, 'how am I going to improve my performance? What do I need from a car?

"'What does the car need from my driving, rather than my opportunity maybe going amiss?'"

[Article continues below]

Driver

George Russell

British

63

Russell concedes to 'reality' of difficult F1 season

Russell managed to close the gap at the midpoint of the season when Antonelli had issues of his own, before the gap ballooned up once again in favour of the Italian.

While Russell acknowledged he has had his share of poor luck, the 28-year-old stated his own performances have not been up to standard in comparison to his team-mate.

"I came from 70 points down to within 25 points post-Silverstone, and then the gap extended," he said.

"Baku happened, that felt pretty big in terms of my chances again, and then of course, one week later, you [get] kicked down again, and salt added to the wound with the grid penalty in Singapore.

"This season just hasn't meant to be. I'm not bitter about it.

"I'll look back on the areas I could have done better and should have done better, as opposed to things that have been out of my control that have gone against me.

"As much [that] has gone against me in terms of bad luck, there's been as much of my performances that haven't been to the scratch that I know I'm capable of.

"That's the reality of it."

title: Charles Leclerc hammers Isack Hadjar with 'nonsense' Max Verstappen response
excerpt:
A swift response from Charles Leclerc to an outrageous claim from Isack Hadjar.

Charles Leclerc has dismissed Isack Hadjar's claim that Max Verstappen would have won the Singapore Grand Prix by a bigger margin had he been driving a Ferrari, branding the suggestion "nonsense".

Hadjar made the remark ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix, downplaying Red Bull's pace advantage and insisting the Milton Keynes-based team did not have the fastest car on the grid in Singapore, despite Verstappen converting pole into victory.

The Dutchman controlled the race from the front at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, managing his tyres to beat Leclerc by 7.335 seconds, with Kimi Antonelli completing the podium for Mercedes.

Leclerc could not get near the four-time F1 champion in the race, and he was left far from impressed when asked about Hadjar's comments.

Speaking to the media, including RacingNews365, ahead of the Circuit of the Americas weekend, Leclerc made clear he felt Hadjar was in no position to judge.

"I think it's nonsense to start saying these kinds of things," said Leclerc.

"I mean, Isack has no idea what kind of car we drive, and I have no idea what kind of car he drives."

[Article continues below]

Leclerc predicts 'very tight' fight

The Ferrari driver finished second in Singapore after struggling to make progress in Verstappen's dirty air, with team-mate Lewis Hamilton fading to sixth after an extended stint on soft tyres that left him exposed in the closing laps.

Looking ahead to Austin, Leclerc was cautious about predicting how the order might shake out, pointing to how tight the field has become across the back end of the season.

"It's such a tight field that it's very, very difficult for us to predict," he said.

"Yes, of course, we kind of have an idea of how we will be on this track, but when you are speaking about such fine margins, it relies really on optimising your package, and that has a much bigger influence than what we expect in terms of the cars.

"The only outlier in the last few races is that maybe we expected Mercedes to be further ahead than they actually were.

"If they manage to finally unlock the performance that we kind of had in mind for them in the last few races, then I think they will be further ahead than any others, but otherwise, it's going to be very tight."

title: Max Verstappen addresses prospect at being forced to take unwanted F1 penalty
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has not ruled out the prospect of being forced to take an engine penalty in the remainder of the 2026 F1 season.

The Red Bull driver has thus far not taken a engine grid penalty in the campaign, and is on the final penalty-free example of the Internal Combustion Engine, turbocharger, MGU-K, energy store, control electronics, and the exhaust systems.

He has also used five of the six permitted power unit ancillary components, meaning he would have to get to seven used before a penalty is incurred.

In contrast, team-mate Isack Hadjar took a five-place grid drop in Malaysia for a new ICE, and took a pit-lane start in Singapore for a new ICE, turbocharger, exhaust, and PU-ANC.

In Italy, Liam Lawson took a full whack penalty of every component and was sent to the back of the field, although this counted towards the total of Hadjar's car with Lawson deputising for the injured Frenchman at the time.

Verstappen has also suffered two power unit related retirements in 2026, with a coolant leak forcing him out in China, before an engine failure off the line in Monaco ended his race on Lap 1.

When asked if a potential penalty was incoming over the final six rounds of the season, Verstappen, who has won the previous two races in Sepang and Singapore, did not rule it out.

"That we have to take a penalty at one point, yeah, potentially," Verstappen told media, including RacingNews365.

"But there's no known date to that at the moment.

"So we just see what happens."
